component_findings.distribution_artifacts: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-1--kotlin): per-package recency_score: 100 if days_since<=30; 90 if <=60; 75 if <=180; 60 if <=365; 30 if <=730; 0 otherwise. final score = arithmetic mean of per-package recency_scores.
component_findings.recent_maintenance: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-1--kotlin): Release-date recency on Maven Central is a maintenance proxy, not a direct measure of code quality or issue-response time; some mature libraries (e.g. kotlinx.coroutines, kotlinx.serialization) intentionally ship less frequently once API-stable while still receiving continuous commit activity upstream, so the measured 100-180 day gaps likely understate true maintenance health for those specific packages. This proxy was collected identically for all languages in this evaluation.

metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.selection_rule: Use the primary package registry/ecosystem for the language when one exists and evaluate current observable maintenance within the fixed activity window; package count alone is never sufficient.

metric.third_party_library_availability_.limitations: Raw popularity indicators (stars, downloads) were not used as a standalone proxy; release-date recency from Maven Central was used as a declared, consistently-collected proxy for currency. Kotlin's full interop with the Java/Maven ecosystem is a structural strength not fully captured by this 10-domain sample; domains such as desktop GUI, ML/data-science, and embedded/bare-metal were excluded from the fixed sample and are comparatively less mature natively in Kotlin than in some other ecosystems.
metric.third_party_library_availability_.selection_rule: Inspect the same five fixed domain groups for every language; prefer the official package index or official ecosystem directory, then independent package/project evidence.
